lines.text: A $30,000 software that Wall Street has depended on for decades just got replaced by a free GitHub repo.
Researchers from Tsinghua University just open-sourced an AI called Kronos, and it's the first foundation model ever built specifically to read the stock market like a language.
Here's what makes this different from every trading bot you've seen.
Kronos doesn't look at charts the way you do.
It takes raw candlestick data, opens, closes, highs, lows, volume, and converts it into tokens.
The same way ChatGPT turns words into tokens, except this isn't reading English.
It's reading the language of financial markets.
Kronos trained on data from over 45 stock exchanges around the world.
Crypto, Forex, equities, and more.
And the model?
Completely free.
Wall Street firms have spent billions building proprietary models like this, and a group of researchers just gave it away.
This is the kind of thing that used to be locked behind hedge fund doors.
Comment Kronos and I'll DM you the link.

notes: **Recreating:** @daniel.cross.ai · https://www.instagram.com/p/Db3P17nN1Og/ · copy its rhythm: a split screen for the first 1.2s (pro trading desk on top, Joshua below) with "$30,000 worth of software" across the middle from frame 1, then 16 fast cuts in the first 5s; full-frame voiceover over phone-filmed real screens and desk B-roll in the middle (face only at the start, on line 4 and at the end); the ChatGPT logo on "ChatGPT"; "FREE" in yellow on the free reveal (their yellow "crypto" move); a second burst of fast desk cuts on lines 13–14; back to Joshua's face for the CTA. **Layout:** 0–1.2s split screen (stock desk clip top half, Joshua bottom half). Then full frame. Phone-filmed screens are filmed on a phone pointed at the laptop, slightly handheld, like the original's README shots (never their footage). **Times** are estimates at Joshua's pace (3.2 words a second, about 57s). Re-time to the real take.

notes: **Presenter:** Joshua. One person, one list, in video order.
**Before recording anything:** Joshua has a Qube login on his laptop. Don't show any API keys, emails, account numbers or file paths.

**Phone-filmed screens** (A3, A6, A7, A9, A10): the original films real screens with a phone, slightly handheld, not as clean screen captures. Do the same: laptop on the desk, Chrome full screen, zoom 125%, no tabs or bookmarks showing, laptop brightness at max, room lights dimmed so there's no glare. Phone vertical (9:16), 20–30cm from the screen, slow and steady.
**Recording order for the Qube clips** (they build on each other): A6 → A7 → A9.

rows.how: 1. Phone vertical (9:16), eye level, office lights on, lock focus and exposure. 2. Frame head and chest, Joshua looking straight at the lens. 3. Record the hook twice, clean. 4. Record lines 1–15 in one take, no pauses between lines (this is also the voiceover for the middle of the video). 5. Move the phone in close (face fills the frame) and record, three times each: "Qube doesn't make you learn to code." · "This is the kind of thing that used to be locked behind hedge fund doors." · "Comment QUBE and I'll send you the link for the free sign-up." Say TQX as letters, "T-Q-X".

Text over the video from frame 1 to 5.9s: "$30,000 worth of software", Inter Bold 96px white with a black 6px stroke, centred across the middle of the frame, "$30,000" in gold #E8B04B. No box behind it.

rows.what: Empty box, then typing the strategy into Qube
rows.how: 1. Logged in to Qube, start a new strategy from plain English. 2. Before typing anything, phone-film the empty plain-English box: 2s of the whole screen, then move the phone slowly closer to the empty box for 2s (this is line 3). **CHECK: no result, return or number on screen in this shot.** 3. Phone-film over his shoulder: his hands on the keyboard (1s), then the screen. 4. Type exactly, by hand, don't paste: `Buy the S&P 500 at the close when it drops 2% in a day. Sell once it's up 2% from where I bought. Put 10% of my account into each trade. Get out if it falls another 3% from where I bought.` 5. Hold 2s on the full sentence before pressing Enter.
rows.file: J024_A6_typing.mp4 · 1080×1920 · up to 40s (sped up in the edit)

rows.how: 1. Press Enter on the A6 sentence. 2. Keep filming until Qube shows the finished strategy. Hold 3s on it. 3. Take one screenshot of the finished strategy. **CHECK: the strategy must cover all four parts of the sentence (when to buy, when to sell, how much, when to get out). If a part is missing, send Mark the screenshot before the edit.**

rows.what: ChatGPT logo, then a ChatGPT email
rows.how: (1) Canva, 1080×1920, dark #0B0F14 background, the ChatGPT logo centred in white, 400px wide. Export PNG. (2) Joshua: open chatgpt.com in Chrome (no sidebar history showing, log out of anything personal or use a fresh chat). Type exactly: `Write a short email asking my manager for Friday off.` Press Enter. Phone-film the answer appearing, 3s. **CHECK: no name, email address or company shows in the answer. If one does, run it again.**

1. On the A7 strategy, set the test to the last five years of prices (or the longest Qube offers if that's shorter). 2. Start filming, run the backtest, film until the result appears and the chart has drawn. 3. Scroll the full trade list top to bottom in about 3s. 4. Take one screenshot of the result. **CHECK: the test must be five years or less (the line says "up to five years"). The trade list must show losing trades as well as winning ones. If it shows none, tell Mark before the edit. No number from this result is spoken or put on screen as a claim.**
